scope: Full actual candidate stems/options read during first0026design; retained as discarded comparison context, not reused final question wording.

records.stem: At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?

choices.text: Dispense because a stimulant prescription remains valid for six months.
Treat the Schedule II prescription as expired under the 30-day Massachusetts validity rule.
Call the prescriber and use that confirmation to restart the 30-day clock.
Transfer the unfilled prescription so the receiving pharmacy can treat it as new.
Apply the one-year Schedule VI transfer period.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy discovers a reportable theft and plans to withhold the initial written DEA notice until a final quantity investigation is complete.

Case B: Staff confuse the current provision's completed electronic Form 106 period with the separate initial-notice deadline.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Only losses above a universal fixed dollar threshold can be significant under the described rule.
A confirmed theft needs no report whenever only a small quantity was taken.
The initial notice may wait until the completed Form 106 deadline.
The retrieved current 21 CFR 1301.76(b) states 45 days after discovery for the complete electronic Form 106.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts methylphenidate prescription was issued 34 days ago. It authorizes a 90-day supply, has never been filled, and is presented for routine outpatient dispensing today.

Which fact prevents dispensing under this prescription? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A 90-day supply of a non-opioid CII is categorically prohibited.
The prescription has passed the Massachusetts 30-day validity period.
Methylphenidate prescriptions are limited to a seven-day supply in every adult.
A previously unfilled CII prescription needs a refill authorization.
